foo5-foo6-walkthrough.title: Foo5 and Foo6: Add Sequential Work and Trace a Call Chain
foo5-foo6-walkthrough.bodyMarkdown:
### Foo5: two loops one after another

The first loop prints `n` pairs while `j` remains `0`. When it finishes, `i == n`. The second loop then prints another `n` pairs while `i` remains `n`.

$$
P(n)=n+n=2n.
$$

The normalized version contains two newline calls, so all `printf` calls total `2n + 2`. Because the loops are sequential rather than nested, their work **adds**. `Foo5` is `Θ(n)`.

### Foo6: one recursive call per level

```c
void Foo6(int n, int i, int j) {
    if (i >= n && j >= n)
        return;
    printf("(%d,%d) ", i, j);
    Foo6(n, i + 1, j + 1);
}
```

Starting from `(0,0)`, the function prints `(0,0)` through `(n−1,n−1)`, then makes one final base-case call at `(n,n)` that does not print.

- tuple prints: `n`
- total function calls: `n + 1`
- maximum active recursive frames: proportional to `n`
- time: `Θ(n)`
- call-stack space: `Θ(n)`

The earlier slide uses equality in the base case and the solution slide uses `>=`. With these starting values and updates, both reach `(n,n)` exactly; the `>=` form is safer.
